page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture. Built upon Ampere Altra processors running at a sustained clock frequency of 2.8 GHz under the KVM hypervisor, the instance delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs alongside 8.0 GB of system memory, providing an exact 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes hardware acceleration for AES cryptography, lacks hardware vector extensions typical of x86 platforms such as AVX, incorporates no local NVMe storage, includes zero bundled public IPv4 addresses, and features a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps with no discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent middle-tier performance on synthetic CPU compute and memory throughput tests alongside lower scores on instructions demanding specialized vector pipelines. Synthetic processing via stress-ng measures 1,824.29 in single-core and 7,275.05 in multi-core metrics, positioning it firmly in the average tier. Memory bandwidth achieves 55.26 GB/sec for uncached 256MB reads and 31.38 GB/sec for uncached writes, while cached small-block reads reach 283.44 GB/sec. Conversely, Geekbench metrics show modest throughput with a single-core score of 1,101.0 and a multi-core score of 3,677.0, accompanied by a PassMark CPU score of 3,205.16 and lower-tier cryptographic benchmark figures.

From an infrastructure and resource efficiency perspective, the dedicated ARM core allocation prevents neighbor contention, offering steady execution for ARM-native workloads without paying a premium for idle memory overhead or bundled local storage. However, the complete absence of local disk drives requires reliance on networked block storage, and the 1 Gbps network baseline bounds I/O-intensive distribution. The ecs.c6r.xlarge is most suitable for ARM64-targeted build runners, microservices, containerized API gateways, and distributed web applications that benefit from predictable compute efficiency over memory density.

It is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance operates without discrete GPUs or local disk storage and relies on a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks show steady mid-tier execution in multi-core stress-ng tests and uncached memory transfers, alongside entry-level results in Geekbench and PassMark CPU suites. Hardware features include ARM AES cryptographic acceleration without x86 vector extensions. With its balanced compute profile and resource footprint, the instance serves ARM-native microservices, continuous integration build jobs, lightweight backend APIs, and web serving workloads.
